text: Figure 2.17: Mappable Element - Independent HW This principle still applies if there are shared data and/or registers if they do not require exclusive access. The global driver status can for example be read atomically . Same applies to status registers which are readable without side effects. From the behavioral point of view, MCAL modules realizing this principle appear to be instantiated multiple times, each instance includes a subset of the mappable elements but using a common code available with global scope. The resulting mapping rule is: An independent hardware element shall be mapped to one core only . Consequently the MCAL module instance operating on the hardware element is mapped to the same core.
